balance.note: Thresholds are heuristics, tested on recorded laps.

suggestions.label: Front Anti-Roll Bar
suggestions.effect: A softer front bar gives more front grip in slow and medium corners, at the cost of slower response and more body roll.
suggestions.why: A softer front bar lets the front tyres take more load in slow corners, where this car pushed wide.
suggestions.hypothesis: Front Anti-Roll Bar 9 -> 7: The car pushed wide in the middle of T4 on 8 of 9 laps, even on your best lap. Expected: A softer front bar gives more front grip in slow and medium corners, at the cost of slower response and more body roll.

suggestions.label: Rear Anti-Roll Bar
suggestions.effect: A stiffer rear bar helps the car rotate and feel agile. It takes grip from the rear, so the car can snap on exits.
suggestions.why: A stiffer rear bar helps the car rotate mid-corner in slow corners.
suggestions.hypothesis: Rear Anti-Roll Bar 6 -> 8: The car pushed wide in the middle of T4 on 8 of 9 laps, even on your best lap. Expected: A stiffer rear bar helps the car rotate and feel agile. It takes grip from the rear, so the car can snap on exits.

setup.caveat: A setup is a starting point, not a guaranteed fix: rule out technique first (braking point, entry speed, brake release, throttle), then change one thing at a time and compare laps.

thresholds.text: A line difference is called out from 1 m (same-driver lap-to-lap spread is 0.7-2.8 m).
Further apart than this is off track or the pit lane, so it is not compared.
Smoothing of the reference line's direction.
Understeer from 3 degrees more slip angle at the front than the rear (real neutral range +0.4 to +2.9).
Oversteer from 1 degree more slip at the rear.
A slide: the car pointing 5 degrees or more away from where it is going, for 0.1 s.
A lock-up: slip ratio -0.20 or lower for 0.1 s.
Wheelspin: rear slip ratio 0.15 or more for 0.2 s with the throttle on.
A balance recurs on at least 2 laps and half the laps with data.
